title: Git & GitHub identity
description: Account-agnostic identity rules. Expected values come from each user's profile (see profile_variables), never from this shared file. When a variable is unset, the rule falls back to a presence / consistency check. Project override (my_finance, macOS): SSH key optional, HTTPS remotes allowed; push uses the default git credential helper (osxkeychain) when no ssh_key is set.

github_user.description: Your GitHub login. gh must be logged in as this account; remotes and gh targets may belong to it.

github_orgs.description: Extra owners (organisations) whose repositories you work on. Comma-separated in the env var.

git_name.description: The commit author name you commit as.

git_email.description: Author email(s) you commit with. Comma-separated in the env var.

ssh_key.description: Path (or path suffix) of the private key network git operations must pin with -i.

rules.name: git-user-name
rules.title: Commit author name is set and expected
rules.description: The effective author name of a commit (from --author, -c user.name=, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME, or git config user.name) must be set. If the profile defines git_name it must equal it.

bad: git commit -m "fix: x"   (user.name unset, or not your git_name)

rules.name: git-user-email
rules.title: Commit author email is set and expected
rules.description: The effective author email must look like an email. If the profile defines git_email it must be one of them (case-insensitive); any regex in patterns is also accepted.

good: git config user.email "<one of your git_email>"
bad: a work email when the profile lists only your personal one

rules.name: ssh-key-pinned
rules.title: Network git operations pin an SSH key
rules.description: push / pull / fetch / clone / ls-remote over SSH must run with an SSH command (GIT_SSH_COMMAND, -c core.sshCommand=, or git config core.sshCommand) that passes -i <key> and every required option. If the profile defines ssh_key, the key path must end with it.

bad: git push origin main   (no core.sshCommand configured)

rules.name: remote-allowed
rules.title: Remotes are SSH remotes on allowed hosts and owners
rules.description: The URL used by clone / remote add / remote set-url, and the URL of the remote used by push / pull / fetch, must be an SSH URL (when require_ssh) on one of hosts. If allowed_owners resolves to a non-empty list, the owner must be in it. Any URL matching extra_patterns is always accepted.

rules.name: gh-active-account
rules.title: gh is logged in as the expected account
rules.description: Before any gh command runs, gh must be logged in on gh_hostname. If the profile defines github_user, the active account (gh auth status --active) must be it. Switch with: gh auth switch --hostname github.com --user <login>.

good: gh auth status  ->  Logged in to github.com account <github_user>
bad: gh auth status  ->  not logged in, or logged in as another account
